name: email-multi-at-pkcs9-dn-attribute-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees rfc822Name is 'example.com' (host-form constraint matching any mailbox at example.com). The leaf has no SAN; its subject DN carries the legacy PKCS#9 emailAddress attribute (OID 1.2.840.113549.1.9.1, IA5String) whose value is 'not@an@email.example.com' — two unquoted '@' characters in one address. RFC 5321 mandates exactly one '@' in a mailbox; the address is malformed and the leaf must be rejected. A validator that parses by 'split at the rightmost @' would extract domain='example.com' (matches constraint) and accept; one that parses by 'split at the leftmost @' would extract domain='an@email.example.com' (doesn't match, malformed); one that gives up on syntax error rejects cleanly.
references: BoringSSL 1616d692 — crypto/x509 nc_email: sync to libpki's logic
notes: Companion to email-multiple-at-raw-san-invalid (SAN side). This case routes through the §4.2.1.10 directive that rfc822Name constraints apply to the subject DN emailAddress attribute when there's no SAN — the same fallback path where Go and Rust already silently no-op (email-pkcs9-dn-embedded-nul-evades-constraint-invalid). Constructed via subject_der_ascii2der because cryptography rejects multi-@ in an IA5String email attribute.

certs.subject: C=US,O=NC Tests,CN=Multi-At DN Leaf
certs.subject_der_ascii2der: SEQUENCE { SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.6 } PrintableString { "US" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.10 } UTF8String { "NC Tests" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.3 } UTF8String { "Multi-At DN Leaf" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 1.2.840.113549.1.9.1 } IA5String { "not@an@email.example.com" } } } }
